newsitem.title: UK: British barley harvest starts amid fine weather.
newsitem.headline: British barley harvest starts amid fine weather.

text.p: Some UK farmers have started barley harvesting after a weekend of sunny weather in most of England but only a small area is involved so far, with many watching the weather and hoping to begin later in the week, farming sources said.
"There are a lot of people out assessing the crop for a start today (Monday)," one source in the central south county of Hampshire said. "If they can get on they will," she said.
Sources in Devon, further west, also said there was barley being cut in their area.
A manager at a cooperative in Hampshire confirmed that there was barley being harvested in the area. "There is, but not very much," he said. "It's just bits and pieces."
"I don't have a handle on the quality and even if I did, it wouldn't be representative of the crop as a whole," he said.
A source at another cooperative, nearer the coast said he had not seen any barley cut yet. But if they weather were to stay fine, he expected to see harvesting getting well under way.
Anything cut so far would be of poor quality, he reckoned.
"We won't see any quantity done until at least the end of the week."
UK forecasters predict summer weather for much of this week, according to the Meteorological Office.

"Drier, warmer and sunnier weather will gradually set in over the weekend, heralding a welcome change for many people that will continue well into next week," the Meteorological Office said in a statement on Friday. --Christopher Lyddon, London newsroom +44 171 542 7928
